**Feature files:** `docs/features/{epub-upload-and-validation,translation-configuration,html-aware-translation-pipeline,job-management-and-persistence,voice-over-generation,workflow-cancellation,navigation-back-to-chooser,demo-translation}.feature` (68 scenarios total; 66 active + 2 defer_combined for Phase 4; the 1 demo scenario carries `@demo` and is excluded from the default e2e runner per the file header — invoked explicitly via `npx playwright test --grep @demo`)

## Schema (per `test-plan-template.md`, D-07 format applied)

- **Test Case ID** — `{REQ-ID}-SC{NN}` (BDD + Playwright) or `{REQ-ID}-UT{NN}` (unit groups) or `F-UT{NN}` (frontend unit groups)
- **Feature ID** — `F1` / `F2` / `F3` / `F5` (from `@feature:F?` tag) or `unit`
- **Description** — scenario name (BDD) or test() title (Playwright) or test module summary (unit)
- **Status** — `Full` (active + green), `Partial` (placeholder / monkeypatched OR `@demo` feature excluded from default e2e runner), `Skipped` (defer-scaling or voiceover), `Stale` (deleted scenario to be removed in plan 02-02), `Pending` (scenario bound in this plan but test code not yet written — F7/F8 tcid-planning pass 2026-07-10; the bdd-test-writer will promote these rows to `Full`/`Partial` as the implementations land)
- **Note** — marker breakdown (`@web`/`@api`/`@integration`/`@smoke`/`@regression`) + binding location (`file:line`)
- **REQ-ID(s)** — the requirement(s) the test proves (JOBS-01..05, CONF-01/02, XLATE-01..03, EPUB-01..03, INFRA-01..04)

## Contract

This Test Plan is the single source of truth for "which test proves which requirement". Downstream plans consume it:

- **Plan 02.1-02** (tcid retrofit) reads each row's Test Case ID + binding location to add `@pytest.mark.tcid("…")` markers (Python) + `test.info().annotations` (Playwright).
- **Plan 02.1-04** (re-record video) reads the Status column to confirm the F2 @smoke scenario is `Full` before re-recording.
- **Plan 03-05** (Phase 3 final BDD + traceability) reads the rows below to add the F4 BDD bindings (9 active + 2 @defer_combined) + the 2 F5 voiceover resume re-bindings (SC05 + SC06) + the new backend unit groups (VOICE-01-UT01..04, VOICE-02-UT05, VOICE-03-UT06..08, VOICE-04-UT09..10) + the 2 frontend unit groups (F-UT01..02) + the 4 Playwright `@web` specs (VOICE-01-SC01..03, VOICE-02-SC01).
- The companion `docs/traceability/requirements-traceability.md` (plan 02.1-01, task 2; updated by plan 03-05) maps every REQ-ID to its test case IDs in this file.

Any new test MUST add its tcid to the relevant section below + the corresponding REQ-ID row in the traceability matrix.

### F7 — Workflow Cancellation (14 rows)

> **REQ-ID note:** All 14 F7 scenarios are tagged `JOBS-06` (Quick 260710-oih / cancel surface REQ-ID added in `.planning/REQUIREMENTS.md` "Job cancel surface" section alongside the `DELETE /api/v1/jobs/{id}` handler at `backend/src/epubtv/api/routers/jobs.py:401-463`). The 14 scenarios are split: **10 backend BDD** (9 `@api` + 1 `@integration`) + **4 Playwright `@web`** scenarios. The 4 @web scenarios (F7-SC01/02/10/14) overlap with F8 (F8-SC03/SC05/SC06) at the assertion level (e.g. SC14 in F7 + SC03 in F8 both check the cancelled-state "Back to Workflow Choice" button); the bdd-test-writer keeps them as distinct tests per the @web/@api split convention (each scenario gets one row in the inventory).
>
> **Gherkin-vs-impl flags (writer/orchestrator must resolve before plan execution):**
>
> - **F7-SC03 + F7-SC05 say HTTP 202**, but the implementation returns **204** (`status_code=204` at `backend/src/epubtv/api/routers/jobs.py:401-403`). The Gherkin `Then the response has HTTP status 202` must change to 204 to match `docs/agents/api-contract.md`.
> - **F7-SC04 expects a `status="cancelled"` WebSocket event within 1 second** but the implementation does `update_status(cancelled)` then `delete_job()` (`jobs.py:461-462`); `JobRepoPort.update_status` only writes the SQLite row and does NOT publish a WS event. Either the cancel handler must emit a WS event (the F5-AC5 6-field envelope with `status="cancelled"`) or the scenario must be re-scoped (e.g. assert the row is gone via GET, no event expected).
> - **F7-SC09 (`expired` terminal-state 409)**: the implementation's terminal-state set is `{"completed", "failed", "cancelled"}` (`jobs.py:444`) — `expired` is NOT in the set, so a DELETE on an expired job would NOT 409. The implementation must add `expired` to the terminal set, OR the scenario must be re-scoped.
> - **F7-SC11 + F7-SC12 use `error.code = "job_cancelled"` (HTTP 410)**, but `backend/src/epubtv/api/error_codes.py` does NOT define `JOB_CANCELLED` (only `JOB_NOT_CANCELLABLE` at line 58). The download router must be extended to emit a 410 `job_cancelled` envelope for a cancelled-but-rows-already-deleted combined job, OR the scenario must change to a different status (e.g. `artifact_not_applicable` 404 — but that conflicts with the spec).
> - **F7-SC13 expects partial artifacts to remain on disk for diagnostics**, but the implementation physically deletes chunks + audio_files on cancel (`jobs.py:462` `delete_job()`). Direct contract conflict — the Gherkin describes retention, the implementation deletes. The writer/orchestrator must choose: (a) implement a "retain partial artifacts on cancel" path in the cancel handler, (b) re-scope the scenario to assert "no further chunks were scheduled after the cancel" (which IS the actual behaviour), or (c) drop the scenario.
> - **F7-SC14 + F8-SC03 (cancelled-state button visibility in the SPA)**: the implementation physically deletes the row on cancel, so the `cancelled` state in the SPA is only briefly observable between `update_status(cancelled)` and `delete_job()`. After the delete, `GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}` returns 404 and `JobStatusPanel` cannot render the cancelled branch. The writer should mock the row to persist (NOT delete) for these two tests so the cancelled state is observable — or re-scope the assertions to check the WS frame's last status before the close.
